nodes.title: SONG STEP SECONDS = FULL GENERATED CLIP / 24
HOW THIS LIVE MUSIC-VIDEO WORKFLOW WORKS
widgets_values:
HOW IT WORKS

The master song is loaded once. Each active clip receives the exact corresponding section of that song encoded into the H3 audio latent. Its audio mask is zero, so diffusion may create matching video but cannot rewrite the song. This is what produces lip sync.

Clip 1 begins from the reference character. Later clips inherit 39 visual context frames from the preceding clip, then crossfade those frames during final assembly.

H3 MUSIC VIDEO CONTROLLER chooses how many sequential clip lanes execute. Last Active preview decodes only the latest clip preview, reducing extra VAE work. The final streaming node decodes one clip at a time, stitches the visual seams, and muxes the untouched master song.

At 15-second clip duration and 39 context frames, each added clip contributes about 13.46 new seconds. Your current song therefore needs about 15 clips.

nodes.title: START HERE — MUSIC VIDEO / LIP-SYNC
widgets_values:
START HERE — AUTOMATIC SONG LENGTH

This copy reads the selected MASTER SONG duration and sets ACTIVE CLIPS automatically.

1. Choose one or two reference images of the same character.
2. Choose the master song.
3. Leave auto_from_song enabled for a complete-song render. The controller label shows the detected duration and calculated clip count.
4. For a short test, disable auto_from_song and set ACTIVE CLIPS manually (usually 1).
5. PREVIEWS changes only the optional per-clip previews; it does not change the final assembled video.

At the current 15-second clip duration and 39 context frames, this 3:19.8 song resolves to 15 active clips. Songs requiring more than the workflow's 20-clip capacity are visibly capped and logged as a warning.

Each clip has its own prompt so scenes can change, but the prompts do not have to be different. Reusing one prompt produces a continuous-performance treatment; changing them lets the music video progress through different shots.

Ultra-realistic cinematic Nordic urban music video. ONE continuous 7-second shot, 24 fps.

REFERENCE IMAGE 1 — RUNA IDENTITY:
RUNA is the only lead singer. Preserve her exact facial identity, facial proportions, eyes, skin texture, blonde braided hairstyle and recognizable appearance throughout.

REFERENCE IMAGE 2 — RUNA OUTFIT:
Grey zip hoodie, fitted white cropped top, loose grey joggers with side stripes, white sneakers, black headphones around her neck. Maintain her original body proportions.

SCENE:
Modern downtown Oslo, Norway, in natural Nordic daylight. RUNA leans against the front hood of a parked dark graphite sports coupe. Four female urban dancers perform behind and beside her. Contemporary Scandinavian architecture, city street and tram tracks remain consistent.

TIMELINE:
0–2s: Medium shot of RUNA leaning against the hood, singing directly to camera with fierce conviction, precise lip-sync and natural expressive gestures. Dancers begin synchronized rhythmic movements behind her.

2–5s: RUNA continues singing, maintaining her position against the car. She subtly moves her shoulders, head and hands to the rhythm. The dancers perform energetic synchronized urban choreography. Camera slowly tracks backward, smoothly and continuously.

5–7s: Camera continues the same gentle backward movement, revealing slightly more of the sports car and dancers. RUNA remains the visual center, singing confidently. Her face remains recognizable and clearly visible.

CAMERA:
ONE SINGLE UNINTERRUPTED SHOT. Smooth, slow, continuous backward dolly movement. No cuts, no inserts, no sudden close-ups, no jump zooms, no abrupt camera movements, no scene transitions. Keep RUNA framed between mid-thigh and head at the widest point. Maintain consistent perspective and spatial continuity.

AUDIO:
Follow the uploaded music exactly. Accurate Norwegian lip-sync, syllable timing and natural mouth articulation. No invented lyrics, no additional singing.

CONSTRAINTS:
ONE RUNA ONLY. No duplicates, no identity drift, no face swaps, no hairstyle changes. Dancers never sing or obstruct her face. Realistic anatomy, natural movement, stable facial details, photorealistic live-action quality.
